notes: Labor hours are approximate book-time estimates, not licensed labor-guide data. Specs marked verify:true must be confirmed against the factory service manual (FSM) before use.

repairs.title: Engine Oil & Filter Change
repairs.interval: Every 5,000 mi / 6 months (severe service) — check maintenance schedule
tools: Floor jack + jack stands or ramps

specs.label: Oil viscosity
specs.value: Factory spec 0W-20 full synthetic (check oil cap / owner's manual)

specs.label: Capacity with filter
specs.value: Approx. 5.1 qt

specs.label: Drain plug torque
specs.value: Approx. 25 ft-lb (34 N·m)

warnings: Never work under a car supported only by a jack.
Hot oil can cause burns — let the engine cool 10–15 minutes after warming.

steps.text: Run the engine for 2–3 minutes to warm the oil so it drains fully, then shut it off.
Raise the front of the car on ramps or jack stands at the factory lift points. Chock the rear wheels.
Open the access panel in the front engine undercover (or remove the undercover fasteners) to expose the drain plug and filter.
Remove the oil fill cap on top of the engine to let the oil drain faster.
Place the drain pan, remove the drain plug and let the oil drain completely.
Remove the oil filter. Wipe the mounting surface clean and make sure the old gasket came off with the filter.
Lightly oil the new filter's gasket and install it hand-tight plus about 3/4 turn (follow the filter's instructions).
Install the drain plug with a NEW crush washer and torque to spec.
Lower the car so it sits level. Fill with the specified oil, starting about 1/2 qt under capacity.
Start the engine, check for leaks at the filter and plug, shut off, wait 2 minutes and check the dipstick. Top off to the full mark.
Reinstall the undercover access panel and reset the oil maintenance reminder in the vehicle settings menu.

repairs.title: Spark Plug Replacement (all 6)
repairs.interval: Factory interval per maintenance schedule; many owners do 30k–40k mi, sooner if tuned
parts: 6x OEM-spec iridium spark plugs (or one step colder if tuned)
tools: Thin-wall spark plug socket (size to match plug)

specs.label: Spark plug torque
specs.value: Approx. 13–15 ft-lb (18–20 N·m) on a clean, dry thread

specs.label: Plug gap
specs.value: Pre-gapped from factory — do not adjust iridium tips

warnings: Only do this on a COLD engine — aluminum heads strip easily when hot.
Blow out each plug well before removing the plug so debris doesn't fall into the cylinder.

steps.text: Make sure the engine is fully cold. Disconnect the negative battery terminal (optional but recommended).
Remove the plastic engine cover (pulls straight up off grommets).
Unplug the electrical connector on each ignition coil. Press the lock tab fully before pulling.
Remove each coil's retaining bolt and pull the coils straight up. Keep them in order by cylinder.
Blow out each spark plug well with compressed air.
Remove one plug at a time with the thin-wall socket and extension. Inspect it — oily, white or heavily sooted plugs point to other problems.
Thread the new plug in BY HAND first (a short rubber hose on the plug end works well) to avoid cross-threading.
Torque each plug to spec. Do not use anti-seize unless the plug manufacturer calls for it (it changes the torque value).
Optionally add a thin film of dielectric grease inside each coil boot, then reinstall coils, bolts and connectors.
Reinstall the engine cover, reconnect the battery, start the engine and confirm it idles smoothly with no check-engine light.

repairs.title: Ignition Coil Replacement
repairs.laborNote: All 6 coils; a single coil is roughly 0.3–0.4 hr
parts: Ignition coil(s) — single coil or full set of 6
warnings: Misfire codes P0301–P0306 tell you which cylinder. Swap the suspect coil to another cylinder to confirm the misfire follows the coil before buying parts.

steps.text: Read codes with an OBD-II scanner and note which cylinder is misfiring.
Remove the engine cover.
Unplug the coil connector, remove the retaining bolt and pull the coil straight up.
Diagnostic swap: move the suspect coil to a different cylinder, clear codes, drive and re-scan. If the misfire moved, the coil is bad.
Install the new coil, seat it fully, install the bolt and plug in the connector until it clicks.
Clear codes, reinstall the engine cover and test drive.

repairs.title: Engine Air Filters (both sides)
repairs.interval: Inspect every oil change; replace roughly every 15k–30k mi
parts: 2x engine air filters (the 3.0t has one air box per turbo/bank)
tools: Screwdriver or socket set (depending on air box fasteners)

steps.text: Open the hood. Locate the two air boxes (driver and passenger side).
Release the clips/screws on the first air box lid and lift it enough to remove the filter.
Note the filter orientation, remove it, and wipe out any debris in the box.
Install the new filter with the same orientation, making sure the seal sits evenly all the way around.
Close and secure the lid. Repeat on the other side.
Empty the glove box and lower it (release the stops/damper on the sides).
Unclip the filter access cover behind the glove box.
Slide out the old filter. Note the airflow arrow direction.
Insert the new filter with the airflow arrow pointing the same way as the old one.
Reinstall the cover and the glove box.

repairs.title: Front Brake Pads & Rotors

specs.label: Lug nut torque
specs.value: 80 ft-lb (108 N·m)

specs.label: Caliper bracket bolts
specs.value: See FSM — depends on caliper (Sport/Red Sport trims use larger multi-piston calipers)

warnings: Brake parts must be confirmed for YOUR trim — Sport/Red Sport brakes are different from base brakes.
Pump the brake pedal several times before driving after pushing pistons back.

steps.text: Loosen lug nuts slightly, raise the front on jack stands and remove the wheels.
Check the brake fluid reservoir — if it's full, remove a little fluid so it doesn't overflow when pistons are pushed back.
Remove the pad retaining pins/clips (multi-piston) or caliper slide bolts (sliding caliper) and remove the old pads.
Remove the caliper bracket (or caliper on fixed calipers) and hang it with wire — don't let it hang by the brake hose.
Remove the rotor. If stuck, use the threaded jacking holes or tap the hat area with a mallet.
Clean the hub face with a wire brush so the new rotor sits flat.
Clean the new rotors with brake cleaner and install them.
Reinstall bracket/caliper with new hardware clips; lubricate slide pins and pad contact points lightly.
Push the pistons back evenly and install the new pads.
Reinstall the wheels and torque lugs to spec in a star pattern.
Pump the pedal until firm, check fluid level, then bed in the pads: several 35→5 mph moderate stops without coming to a full stop.

repairs.title: Rear Brake Pads & Rotors
repairs.laborNote: Pads only is roughly 1.0 hr; add time if parking brake shoes need adjusting
tools: Flat screwdriver / brake spoon (parking brake adjuster)

specs.label: Lug nut torque
specs.value: 80 ft-lb (108 N·m)

warnings: Release the parking brake before removing rotors.
The rear rotor has a drum-in-hat parking brake on many trims — if the rotor won't come off, back off the parking brake shoe adjuster.

steps.text: Chock the front wheels, release the parking brake, raise the rear on jack stands and remove the wheels.
Remove the caliper (or pad pins on multi-piston calipers) and remove the old pads.
Remove the caliper bracket and hang the caliper with wire.
Remove the rotor. If it binds on the parking brake shoes, back off the adjuster through the access hole.
Inspect the parking brake shoes while the rotor is off.
Clean the hub, install the new rotor, bracket and hardware.
Retract the piston, install new pads and the caliper.
Adjust the parking brake shoes if needed per FSM procedure.
Reinstall wheels, torque lugs, pump the pedal until firm and bed in the pads.

repairs.title: Brake Fluid Flush / Bleed
parts: DOT 3 brake fluid (check reservoir cap for spec), 1 liter

specs.label: Bleed order
specs.value: Typically farthest from master cylinder first: RR, LR, RF, LF — confirm in FSM

warnings: Brake fluid strips paint — cover painted surfaces and rinse spills with water immediately.
Never let the reservoir run dry while bleeding or you'll get air in the ABS unit.

steps.text: Remove old fluid from the reservoir with a baster and refill with fresh fluid.
Raise the car and remove the wheels (or reach the bleeders through the wheel).
Starting at the first wheel in the bleed order, attach tubing to the bleeder into a catch bottle.
Have a helper press and hold the pedal, open the bleeder, close it, then release the pedal. Repeat until clean fluid with no bubbles comes out.
Top up the reservoir frequently. Repeat at each wheel in order.
Torque bleeders snugly (don't overtighten), fill reservoir to MAX, confirm a firm pedal before driving.

repairs.title: 12V Battery Replacement
parts: 12V battery (match group size, CCA and type — AGM if originally AGM)
warnings: Always disconnect NEGATIVE first and reconnect it LAST.
After replacement you may need to re-initialize auto up/down windows and the sunroof.

steps.text: Turn everything off and remove the key/fob from the car.
Locate the battery and remove any covers or trim over it.
Disconnect the negative (−) terminal, then the positive (+) terminal.
Remove the hold-down bracket and lift the battery out (it's heavy — lift with your legs).
Clean the terminals and tray. Install the new battery in the same orientation.
Install the hold-down, connect positive (+) then negative (−).
Start the car, then re-initialize power windows (hold switch down past auto, then up past auto and hold a few seconds) and sunroof if needed.

repairs.title: Engine Coolant Drain & Fill
parts: Nissan/Infiniti Long Life Antifreeze (blue) or compatible, premixed 50/50

specs.label: Coolant type
specs.value: Infiniti Long Life Coolant (blue), 50/50 premix

warnings: Never open the cooling system when hot.
The 3.0t has a SEPARATE low-temperature coolant loop for the intercoolers — this procedure is for the main engine loop. See the intercooler coolant job for that loop.
Coolant is toxic to pets — clean up spills.

steps.text: Make sure the engine is fully cold. Remove the radiator cap.
Raise the front and remove the undercover to reach the radiator drain cock.
Open the radiator drain and drain into the pan. Close the drain when empty.
Fill slowly through the radiator with the specified coolant (spill-free funnel helps burp air).
Open any air bleed points per FSM, start the engine with heater on HOT and let it reach operating temperature, topping off as bubbles rise.
Shut off, let it cool, top off the radiator and the reservoir to the MAX/FULL line.
Recheck the level after the next couple of drives.

repairs.title: Intercooler (Low-Temp) Coolant Drain & Fill
parts: Infiniti-spec coolant for the intercooler circuit, premixed
tools: OBD-II scan tool capable of running the intercooler pump (helpful for bleeding)
warnings: The intercooler loop has its own reservoir and electric pump — air in this loop raises intake temps and costs power.
Confirm the drain location and bleed procedure in the FSM for your year.

steps.text: With the engine cold, locate the intercooler coolant reservoir (separate from the main engine reservoir).
Raise the car, remove the undercover, and drain from the lowest point of the intercooler circuit (low-temp radiator).
Refill through the intercooler reservoir slowly.
Run the electric intercooler pump (key on / scan tool activation) to circulate coolant and purge air, topping off as the level drops.
Recheck the level after a test drive once everything has cooled.

repairs.title: Automatic Transmission Fluid Drain & Fill (7-speed)
parts: Infiniti-specified ATF (Matic S per most references — verify)
tools: Jack + jack stands (car must be LEVEL)
OBD-II scan tool that reads ATF temperature

specs.label: Fluid type
specs.value: Nissan Matic S ATF

specs.label: Level check temperature
specs.value: Check at the FSM-specified ATF temperature window

warnings: This transmission has no dipstick — the level MUST be set at the correct fluid temperature with the car level, or you risk over/underfilling.
A single drain & fill replaces only part of the fluid; repeat for a fuller exchange.

steps.text: Raise the car level on four jack stands.
Remove the drain plug and drain the fluid. Measure how much came out.
Reinstall the drain plug with a new washer.
Remove the fill/overflow plug and pump in roughly the amount you drained.
Start the engine, cycle through gears with the brake held, and monitor ATF temperature with the scan tool.
At the specified temperature, with the engine running, open the overflow — fluid should just trickle out. Add fluid until it does.
Reinstall the fill plug with a new washer and torque to spec.

repairs.title: Rear Differential Fluid
parts: Gear oil per FSM spec (GL-5, approx. 1–1.5 qt — verify)

specs.label: Fluid
specs.value: GL-5 gear oil, viscosity per FSM

warnings: ALWAYS loosen the FILL plug first — if you drain it and can't open the fill plug, you're stuck.

steps.text: Raise the car level.
Break loose the FILL plug first.
Remove the drain plug and drain the fluid. Clean the magnetic plug.
Reinstall the drain plug with a new gasket.
Pump fluid into the fill hole until it starts to run out.
Reinstall the fill plug with a new gasket.

repairs.title: Accessory Drive Belt
tools: Belt tensioner tool or long-handle ratchet
Phone camera (photo the belt routing first)
warnings: Take a photo of the belt routing BEFORE removing the old belt.

steps.text: Photograph the belt routing (there's often a diagram on a sticker under the hood).
Remove the undercover / any covers blocking access to the tensioner.
Rotate the tensioner to relieve tension and slip the belt off one pulley, then remove it.
Spin each pulley by hand and check for noise, wobble or roughness (tensioner and idler).
Route the new belt per the diagram, leaving one smooth pulley for last, then release the tensioner.
Verify the belt is seated in every groove, then start the engine and watch it run for a minute.

repairs.title: Front Compression/Tension Rod (bushing clunk)
repairs.laborNote: Per side; alignment recommended afterwards (~1.0 hr)
parts: New nuts if specified as one-time-use

specs.label: Bushing bolt torque
specs.value: Tighten with the car at ride height (weight on wheels) — torque per FSM

warnings: Final-tighten rubber bushings with the suspension loaded at ride height, or the new bushing will be pre-twisted and wear early.

steps.text: Raise the front, support on stands and remove the wheel.
Remove the undercover pieces in the way.
Remove the nut from the ball joint end and separate it from the steering knuckle.
Remove the frame-side bushing bolt and remove the rod.
Install the new rod, ball joint nut torqued to spec, frame bolt snug only.
Lower the car or jack the hub to ride height, then torque the bushing bolt.
Reinstall the wheel and get an alignment.

repairs.title: Boost Leak / Charge Pipe Inspection
parts: Boost leak tester adapter (DIY or purchased)

specs.label: Test pressure
specs.value: Keep test pressure low (~15–20 psi) and never leave unattended

warnings: Do not start the engine with the boost leak tester installed.
Engine valves may be open on a cylinder — some air escaping out the exhaust or crankcase is normal.

steps.text: Symptoms to look for: underboost codes, hissing under load, power loss, fluttering sounds.
Remove the engine cover and visually inspect charge pipes, couplers and clamps between turbos, intercoolers and throttle body.
Install the boost leak tester at the turbo inlets (one side at a time on twin-turbo).
Pressurize slowly to the test pressure and listen. Spray soapy water on joints — bubbles show leaks.
Repair any leaking couplers/clamps, retest, and clear codes.

repairs.title: Tire Rotation

specs.label: Lug nut torque
specs.value: 80 ft-lb (108 N·m)

specs.label: Rotation pattern
specs.value: Staggered setups (different front/rear sizes) can only swap side-to-side if non-directional

warnings: If your car has a staggered wheel/tire setup, you cannot rotate front-to-rear.

steps.text: Loosen all lug nuts a half turn with the car on the ground.
Raise and support the car.
Rotate front-to-rear on the same side (square setups with directional tires), or per the tire manufacturer's pattern.
Snug lug nuts, lower the car, torque in a star pattern.
Set tire pressures to the door-jamb placard and reset the TPMS if needed.

repairs.title: Engine Oil & Filter Change

specs.label: Oil type & capacity
specs.value: See owner's manual / oil cap

warnings: Never work under a car supported only by a jack.

steps.text: Warm the engine briefly, then shut it off.
Safely raise the car and locate the drain plug and filter.
Drain the oil, then replace the filter (oil the new gasket).
Reinstall the drain plug with a new washer.
Refill with the specified oil, run the engine, check for leaks, recheck the dipstick.
Reset the oil life monitor.

repairs.title: Front Brake Pads & Rotors

specs.label: Lug nut torque
specs.value: See owner's manual

warnings: Pump the brake pedal before driving.

steps.text: Raise the car and remove the front wheels.
Remove the caliper and bracket; hang the caliper with wire.
Replace the rotor and pad hardware.
Compress the piston, install pads and caliper.
Torque everything to spec, pump the pedal, bed in the pads.

repairs.title: 12V Battery Replacement
warnings: Disconnect negative first, reconnect negative last.

steps.text: Disconnect negative, then positive.
Remove the hold-down and old battery.
Clean terminals, install the new battery.
Connect positive, then negative. Reset windows/clock as needed.
Open the air box.
Replace the filter in the same orientation.
Close the air box securely.
Access the filter (usually behind the glove box).
Replace it, matching the airflow arrow.
Reassemble.

repairs.title: Spark Plug Replacement
repairs.laborNote: Varies widely: ~0.8 hr on an easy 4-cyl to 3+ hr on some V6/V8s

specs.label: Gap & torque
specs.value: Per plug manufacturer / FSM

warnings: Work on a cold engine.

steps.text: Remove coils or plug wires.
Blow out plug wells, remove plugs.
Thread new plugs by hand, torque to spec.
Reinstall coils/wires.
Loosen lugs, raise the car.
Rotate per the tire manufacturer's pattern.
Torque lugs, set pressures.

repairs.title: Brake Fluid Flush
warnings: Brake fluid damages paint.

steps.text: Replace reservoir fluid with fresh fluid.
Bleed each wheel, farthest from master cylinder first.
Keep the reservoir topped up; confirm a firm pedal.
